summary.headline: Hikal Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 403 crore, EBITDA margin 9.2%, PAT Rs (-7) crore; management guides FY27 revenue growth 14-16% and EBITDA growth 25-30%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs 403 crore with EBITDA of Rs 37 crore (9.2% margin) and PAT of Rs (-7) crore, aided by Rs 9 crore exceptional income from reversal of a Labour Code provision. Pharma grew year-on-year despite a planned shutdown for US FDA remediation, while Crop Protection was mixed, with domestic own-product volumes improving but CDMO export orders deferred. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 14-16% revenue growth and 25-30% EBITDA growth, with momentum expected to build in H2. Net debt was cut to Rs 685 crore by FY26 end (from Rs 815 crore in FY24), and debt-to-equity was 0.53.

financial_highlights.change: Reversal of excess Q4 FY26 provision for new Labour Codes

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 233 crore, EBIT Rs 8 crore (3.2% margin); Panoli and Bangalore plants ran at about 55-60% utilisation including Q1 shutdown. Management expects pharma to grow 18-19% CAGR going forward.

segments.name: Crop Protection
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 170 crore, EBIT Rs (-6) crore. Own products grew sequentially on domestic demand; CDMO exports subdued as some orders deferred to H2. Management expects flattish-to-marginal growth this year and mid-to-high single digit growth longer term.

segments.name: Animal Health
segments.commentary: Annual turnover above Rs 100 crore in FY26; management targets Rs 400 crore plus by FY30 and 20%+ EBITDA margin at scale. Completed US EPA and Canada PMRA filings for one molecule in Q1.

segments.name: Personal Care (new)
segments.commentary: Dedicated line at Panoli commercial production commenced; revenue expected by end of this year (launch year, small volumes). Management targets over Rs 200 crore revenue within about three years post-FY27 at over 20% EBITDA margin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at approximately 14-16%, with strong growth in pharma and marginal growth in crop.
FY27 EBITDA growth guided at approximately 25-30%.
Q2 expected to show substantial YoY growth in revenue and EBITDA; H2 FY27 momentum expected to accelerate.
FDA remediation costs weigh on fixed costs in FY27; benefit expected from next year, with FY28 described as substantially better.
Management expects 15-16% CAGR to continue beyond FY27.
Crop Protection: Q2 expected better than Q1 (Kharif), Q3 further improvement (Rabi and Latin America); crop margins to stay under pressure near term.
capex_capacity: Over the last 4 years, about Rs 900 crore capex: Rs 300 crore maintenance (about Rs 75 crore a year across 6 sites) and Rs 600 crore growth.
Rs 300 crore agrochemical plant partly impaired in Q4 FY26 is being retooled into a multipurpose pharma and Animal Health CDMO facility, cutting execution timelines by about 12 months.
New cGMP pilot plant at Pune R&D centre and Panoli pilot plant commissioned; DMF filing capacity expected to rise from 2-3 to 5-7 filings per year.
Q1 capex of Rs 45 crore for de-bottlenecking, regulatory upgrades and new capacity; capex in crop business kept minimal.
demand_pricing: Crop Protection: global channel destocking largely complete, but distributors still buying just in time; crop pricing under pressure from Chinese oversupply.
Raw material and energy costs rose on Middle East geopolitical tensions; crop Q1 margin hit of about Rs 7-8 crore from raw material increases.
Some crop contracts have pass-through clauses; others only partially compensate for cost increases.
Pharma: customer ordering patterns normalising; zero lost customer contracts in last 12 months per management; 86+ customer audits re-approved facilities.
Pharma CDMO pipeline of around 8-9 NCE/intermediate molecules; repeat campaign orders from innovators; discussions with a leading Japanese innovator progressing.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin should be expected for Animal Health?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 20%+ EBITDA margin for Animal Health once operating leverage is reached.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 3-year outlook for Crop Protection?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects marginal growth now, moving to mid-to-high single-digit growth; no significant new capital going into crop, and new CDMO contract margins are lower than 3-4 years ago.

qa_highlights.question: Is Hikal positioning as a pharma company over the next five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management expects pharma, allied pharma and Personal Care to be about 70-80% of revenue in 2-3 years, with crop about 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Why aren't FY27 margins higher given pharma and Animal Health growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 is a transition year with FDA remediation costs in fixed costs; the meaningful margin improvement is expected in FY28 and beyond.

qa_highlights.question: How will FDA clearance affect FY28 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Pending filings awaiting FDA approval are expected to be executed after re-inspection, ramping revenue in FY28 at better margins.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of clearing the US FDA re-inspection this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes for re-inspection by end of FY27, with possible delays of a few months; a few open issues remain to be closed in the next few months.

risks_watch: Timing of US FDA re-inspection (targeted by end FY27, may slip a few months); remediation costs continue to weigh on fixed costs.
Crop pricing pressure from China and raw material/energy volatility linked to Middle East geopolitics; management said costs could rise again if the conflict resumes.
Deferred CDMO orders in crop and pharma shifting from H1 to H2, increasing dependence on H2 execution.
Personal Care and Animal Health ramp-up depends on new contracts and validations; Personal Care revenue only from year-end.
Q1 PAT loss of Rs (-7) crore despite Rs 9 crore exceptional gain; watch for underlying profitability.
